stated: Ensure a sustainable future for football clubs and give fans a stronger voice by: Establishing the promised new independent regulator, placing it on a statutory footing, and giving it the power to impose a fairer financial flow that rewards well-run clubs. Strengthening the propriety test for prospective owners and directors by including human rights questions. Requiring all clubs to have equality, diversity and inclusion action plans.

bearing_set.reason: The mandatory EDI action plans for all clubs and the strengthened human rights-inclusive propriety test for owners directly bear on the equal treatment / anti-discrimination indicator within O9; these are substantive anti-discrimination obligations, not merely sectoral governance.

Football clubs are primary community anchors; the policy's central aim — statutory regulation to ensure club sustainability — directly protects community institutions underpinning social trust, civic participation and local belonging.

membership_note: The two real bearings are O15 (community cohesion via club sustainability) and O9 (equal treatment via mandatory EDI plans and human-rights proprietor test). Potential O14 bearing (fairer financial flows redistributing from richer to poorer clubs) was considered but the stated mechanism rewards 'well-run clubs' rather than explicitly redistributing by wealth/region, so the inequality-reduction mechanism is too ambiguous to clear the non-negligible bar. O13 (football industry prosperity) and O4 (club employment) are real but indirect and niche relative to the fundamentals' aggregate indicators.
